title: itembank evidence event
description: One line of _evidence/evidence.jsonl, built by evidence.response_event() and written by evidence.append_event() alone. additionalProperties is false and every key below is required, so a missing key is a validation failure rather than a shrug: a consumer must be able to tell 'not captured' from 'this field did not exist in that era', and that only works if every key is always present. This document's required/properties describe the response event shape only. event_type may also carry mark, retraction, day_tick, term_lookup or key_review; those get real event bodies from evidence.retraction_event() (plan 01-07), evidence.mark_event() (plan 01-09), evidence.day_tick_event() (plan 01-10), evidence.term_lookup_event() (plan 03.1-02) and evidence.key_review_event() (plan 03.1-03), described in $defs below, but are not yet enforced by the required/properties above -- a retraction, mark, day_tick, term_lookup or key_review line in evidence.jsonl does not validate against this top-level document.

event_id.description: A uuid4 hex identifying this event

event_type.description: This build writes only 'response'. 'retraction' was given a body in plan 01-07, 'mark' in plan 01-09, 'day_tick' in plan 01-10, 'term_lookup' in plan 03.1-02, and 'key_review' in plan 03.1-03.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC to millisecond precision, matching evidence.utc_now()

item_id.description: The opaque [ID:] identity field when assigned (plan 01-04); empty string on an item that has never had id-assign run against it

item_ref.description: The Qn-derived positional id, always present regardless of whether item_id has been assigned

bank.description: The bank file's basename only, never an absolute path (T-1-06) -- a consumer should not expect a resolvable path here

subject.description: The text before the first ':' in a namespaced objective (evidence.subject_of); empty string on an unnamespaced or empty objective

mode.description: Captured live on every surface; this is what makes a drill-mode correct distinguishable from an exam-mode correct. 'legacy' is written only by itembank migrate (plan 01-11), for an imported record whose source (an attempt markdown file, which never recorded a mode) carries no mode of its own.

attempt_number.description: One more than the count of prior response events for this session and this item

answer.description: The learner's raw response, shaped per item type -- a string, an array, or an object

canonical.description: evidence.idempotency_canon()'s output: runtime.canonical_response() when it returns one, or 'short:' + sha256 of the whitespace-collapsed, lowercased answer text when canonical_response() returns null (a short item has no canonical form of its own). This is the same value fed into dedupe_key, so the two can never compare against different things (D-17, plan 01-07); never null.

score.description: true, false, or null for a constructed response not yet marked -- not-yet-marked and marked-wrong are different states

response_time_ms.description: Captured live; milliseconds between the item being served and the response being submitted; null only when the session carries no served_ts.

confidence.description: Captured live where the surface offers it (submit --confidence); null when the learner did not say, which is different from low confidence.

error_category.description: Reserved, always null in schema version 1. No error taxonomy exists; it depends on the tutoring work in Phases 6 and 8. A guessed category would be recorded as fact and read as fact by later trend work, so it is recorded as unknown instead.

hint_tier.description: Reserved, always null in schema version 1. The hint ladder is Phase 6. Null means no ladder existed, which is a different fact from 'the ladder existed and the learner reached tier 0'; conflating them is unrecoverable once written.

review_state.description: 'n/a' for an auto-scored item, 'pending' for a constructed response awaiting a marker, 'marked' once a mark event lands.

dedupe_key.description: A sha256 hex digest identifying one attempt at one item in one session

source_ref.description: Null for a live-path response event. For an event imported by itembank migrate (plan 01-11), an object naming where the record came from and how its item_id was resolved -- never a guess left unstated (D-14).

kind.description: Which legacy store this record came from

path.description: The legacy source file's basename only, never a full path

ref.description: The reference identifying this record within its source file -- an attempt file's item heading number, or a session file's array-index-plus-item_id

resolution.description: 'unresolved' by default (item_id is empty string); 'position' only when --resolve-by-position matched this record's positional reference against today's bank by current item number

mark_event.description: The mark event's real shape (plan 01-09, D-12): a first-class, timestamped fact about a response event, appended alongside it and never a mutation of it -- the response event's own score stays null forever, and review_state is computed at read time from evidence.marks_by_event(), never written back. Not yet wired into a top-level oneOf with the response shape above, so this remains descriptive rather than enforced against a raw evidence.jsonl line.

item_id.description: The opaque [ID:] identity field copied from the response event being marked, empty string when that item has never had id-assign run against it

item_ref.description: The Qn-derived positional id copied from the response event being marked

marks_event.description: The event_id of the response event this mark is about

verdict.description: true for pass, false for fail -- dichotomous, matching every other scored surface in this tool; PARTIAL exists only in GRADING.md's procedure to describe an answer, never to award half credit

marker.description: Always 'human' in this phase; a model verdict is not accepted evidence until Phase 8 (TEACH-09)

dedupe_key.description: sha256 over (session_id, marks_event, verdict, a canonical encoding of rubric), so replaying an identical batch reports already_recorded and a corrected verdict or rubric always records a new, live mark

retraction_event.description: Reserved shape for a retraction event -- D-10's compensating-append undo, given a real body by evidence.retraction_event() in plan 01-07 (retracts/reason/actor/dedupe_key alongside the standard envelope). Not yet wired into a top-level oneOf with the response shape above, so this remains descriptive rather than enforced against a raw evidence.jsonl line.

day_tick_event.description: The day_tick event's real shape (plan 01-10): a lane marked done on a date, appended by the day POST route rather than mutating daily_log.md in place. Not yet wired into a top-level oneOf with the response shape above, so this remains descriptive rather than enforced against a raw evidence.jsonl line.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD and a real calendar date; evidence.day_tick_event() rejects anything else with a ValueError

lane.description: One of surfaces/day.py's DAY_LANES; validated by the day POST route before this event is built, not by evidence.py itself

source.description: Always 'day' in this build -- reserved for a future non-interactive ticker

dedupe_key.description: sha256 over (date, lane) alone, so ticking the same lane on the same date twice always reports already_recorded

term_lookup.description: The term_lookup event's real shape (plan 03.1-02, D-19): a learner looked up a lesson term's definition; it is not a response and carries no score key. Not yet wired into a top-level oneOf with the response shape above, so this remains descriptive rather than enforced against a raw evidence.jsonl line.

bank.description: The bank file's basename only, never an absolute path (T-1-06)

term_slug.description: The lesson_slug() value of the term whose definition was looked up

source.description: reader for the lesson reader path, session for a sitting path -- provenance is append-only and cannot be added later (UI-SPEC §8.5)

actor.description: The acting party; 'learner' in this build

dedupe_key.description: sha256 over (session_id, bank, term_slug, source, mode), so replaying an identical lookup reports already_recorded

key_review.description: The key_review event's real shape (plan 03.1-03, D-19): a learner asked to add a [!KEY] card to review; it is not a response and carries no score key. Phase 10 replays these events into scheduler state. Not yet wired into a top-level oneOf with the response shape above, so this remains descriptive rather than enforced against a raw evidence.jsonl line.

bank.description: The bank file's basename only, never an absolute path (T-1-06)

key_id.description: The [!KEY] block's minted [ID:] value, resolved against the bank's parsed key blocks

actor.description: The acting party; 'learner' in this build

dedupe_key.description: sha256 over (session_id, bank, key_id, mode), so replaying the same review request reports already_recorded
